Against an anaguma guarded by three golds and silvers, the side with two golds is hard to break. The edge file, held only by the weaker silver, knight and lance, is the target.

Jumping the knight to the edge-adjacent square straight away fails, because a pawn push traps it. The basic start is to sacrifice the edge pawn and then drop a 垂れ歩 two squares in front of the defender's edge (▲9四歩△同歩▲9三歩).

The defender can take the 垂れ歩 three ways. Taking with the knight is best for the attacker: run the lance up, or, with two pawns in hand, a second sacrifice and pawn drop traps the knight that just jumped.
Taking with the lance: the knight jumps to attack it. If the silver recaptures, dropping a second lance behind the first (香の重ね打ち) and releasing both lances breaks the file.
Taking with the silver: the knight jumps to threaten the silver, then the pawn drop on the same square is repeated.

The result: once the edge pieces are stripped away, the gold pair on the second file from the edge becomes a wall that blocks the king's escape. A small number of pawns in hand decides which branch works.

Attacks on Mino at its corner (71) or its kobin often win at once. Edge attacks usually build a small advantage step by step instead of crashing through.

The basic edge attack on Mino is a knight jump that attacks the defender's lance. Once the lance can be taken at any time, the attacker can hold that capture back and combine it with threats elsewhere (on 71 and 73).

There are two ways after the edge-pawn sacrifice: 叩き (striking the lance head on the second rank) or 垂れ (a pawn on the third rank). The 垂れ often saves the striking pawn for later. Which one works depends on tempo and on the defender's alternatives.
敵の打ちたいところへ打て: dropping first on the square where the defender wants a blocking pawn means a later lance run cannot be met with a pawn drop.
If the king steps up to the edge square, it occupies the square where the defender would drop a pawn, so the lance run cannot be blocked.
With no pawns in hand, do not sacrifice the edge pawn, because there is no follow-up. Jump the knight first, then plunge it in with promotion. Each recapture leads to a different break.
A knight jumped to the defender's third rank on the edge is a bad shape for the defender. The lance can run at it at any time, and the squares near the king become thin.

Against 4六銀・3七桂, the defender usually answers the attacker's edge pawn push, so the edge pawns face each other (突き合い).

When the attacker has pushed past (突き越し, pawn on the fifth rank), a knight can plunge to the edge square with promotion. A further edge push then almost forces the capture. The attacker attacks easily.
With the pawns facing each other, the defender may ignore the edge push and counterattack, and the knight plunge is no longer available. The attacker's job is harder.
Timing of the edge sacrifice is delicate. Too early, and the defender recaptures and counterattacks by pushing the edge pawn further. Too late, and the defender simply ignores it.
Taking in the edge pawn (取り込み) is a lasting gain when the defender has no pawn left to block. The promotion threat on the edge stays available for the rest of the game.

After the edge pawn is sacrificed, a 垂れ歩 on the edge, then knight-for-lance trades and a second lance dropped behind the first, puts two lances on the edge file and gives a strong file attack.
The proverb 香は下段から打て has exceptions. Dropping the lance one rank higher can stop a defender's knight drop and leaves room for the rook to support from behind.

The same 垂れ歩 can lose effect depending on whose turn it is. With the pawns facing each other rather than pushed past, the defender gains a tempo to counter. Pushed-past pawns favour the attacker, and facing pawns favour the defender.

Behind a rook-and-lance battery on the edge, plainly exchanging pawn, rook and lance on the edge fails, because the defender drops a rook back into the attacker's camp.

The working version is the edge-pawn sacrifice, a 垂れ歩, and a bishop sacrifice on the edge square after the lance takes. The rook then runs up the edge, and a pawn on the fourth rank threatens promotion that cannot be stopped.

Defender's tesuji: drop a pawn first on the square where the attacker wants to drop (敵の打ちたいところへ打て). Then escape early with the king and pull a silver back into the vacated space, which blunts the rook promotion.

Lesson: the edge breakthrough is not a guaranteed win against accurate defence. The attacker should pick between a slow silver-supported version and the fast bishop-sacrifice version according to the 田楽刺し and fork chances elsewhere.

Formation: lance on 1七, rook on 1八, bishop on 6八 or 7九 aiming at 1三, and a knight to 2五 aiming at 1三. It is a single-point breakthrough on the edge.
Defences: answer the edge pawn early, cover 2五 with a silver on 2四, move the king off the edge (菊水矢倉 with the king on 2一, or the king on 3一/4一), or ignore the edge and counterattack in the centre.

facts: Only the first 100k of 158k characters were read, through WebFetch, for term definitions.
突き越し (突き越す): taking 位 (space) with an edge pawn. The 位取り entry notes that for edge pawns the word is 突き越し rather than 位取り.
端歩: a pawn on the 1st or 9th file. 端玉: a king on the 1st or 9th file above the lance, excluding the corner squares.

垂れ歩: a pawn dropped on the enemy's 2nd–4th rank, where it can promote next. 継ぎ歩: a pawn strike repeated right after a sacrifice or a strike. 突き捨て: pushing a pawn so that it is captured. 手抜き: ignoring a threat and playing elsewhere.
田楽刺し: a lance dropped onto a file where valuable pieces stand in a row, winning the one behind.

Proposed unit: id `attack-edge`, file data/lessons/units/attack-edge.json. order 445: free, between attack-kinmusou 440 and endgame-yose 450. path ["上達のためのテクニック","囲い崩し"]. Working title ja 「端攻めは歩の枚数と取り方で決まる」 / en "Edge Attacks Depend on Pawns in Hand and the Recapture". Intro: 端攻め works because castled kings sit near the edge and the edge is guarded by weaker pieces (lance, knight, silver). Whether it succeeds depends on three things: whether the edge pawn is pushed past or facing, how many pawns are in hand, and which piece recaptures. All chapters are kind "position" with independently composed SFENs. Mirror the attack file or the learner's side compared with the JSA columns: they attack gote on the 9筋 for anaguma and Mino and use sente on the 1筋 for Yagura. Do not reproduce any column diagram, mirrored or otherwise. Check each SFEN against .cache/old and run `bun scripts/lessons/check-unit.ts attack-edge --engine`. references: Wikipedia 端攻め/将棋の格言/雀刺し/将棋用語一覧 (CC BY-SA 4.0, adapted:false), and the five JSA columns (All rights reserved, adapted:false, consulted only).

Ch1 「突き越した端歩は一歩で垂れ歩を作る」 (pushed past vs facing):
- Mechanism: with the attacker's pawn on the fifth rank and the defender's on its third, one pawn in hand gives 突き捨て → 垂れ歩 on the defender's second rank (for example ▲1四歩△同歩▲1三歩), and the promotion threat cannot be ignored. With the pawns facing each other (1六/1四), the push ▲1五歩 can be ignored or answered by a counter-push.
- Original position: gote king on 2二 inside a compact 3二金/3一銀 shape, with 香1一 and 桂2一. Sente has 香1九, 飛1八 or 飛2八, 1 pawn in hand, and no other attackers near the edge, to keep the counting clear. Main line: pushed-past pawns. Variation from step 0: the same material with the pawns on 1六/1四, showing that gote plays a different useful move (手抜き) and the edge goes nowhere.
- Label the gote replies as examples, not forced moves.

Ch2 「垂れ歩の取り方を三つに分けて読む」 (端玉には端歩 against anaguma):
- Mechanism: after the sacrifice and 垂れ歩 the defender can take with the lance, knight or silver. Each piece that leaves opens a different weakness:
  - 同桂: the lance runs up, and a second sacrifice traps the knight;
  - 同香: the knight jumps to hit the lance;
  - 同銀: the knight forks or threatens the silver.
- Original position: gote anaguma on the 1筋 (玉1一, 香1二, 桂2一, 銀2二, 金3二, plus a 金3三 or a 4筋 gold, different from the JSA two-golds-on-7筋 shape). Sente has 歩1五, 香1九, 桂 on 3七 or in hand, and 2 pawns in hand.
- Main line: one recapture. Two variations from the 垂れ歩 step, one for each other recapture. Each branch ends on a position where the learner can count that the edge guard has thinned, not on a forced mate. Verify every branch with the engine. Show only branches the engine does not mark as blunders for the attacker.

Ch3 「歩がなければ突き捨てない：桂で香を狙う」 (Mino; pieces in hand decide):
- Mechanism: against Mino, a knight attacking the edge lance is the basic idea, and holding back the lance capture keeps options open. With zero pawns in hand the sacrifice has no follow-up, so the knight jumps first. With pawns in hand, choosing 叩き or 垂れ saves a pawn for 「敵の打ちたいところへ打て」.
- Original position: the learner plays gote attacking sente's Mino on the 1筋. Sente: 玉2八, 銀3八, 金4九, 金5八, 桂2九, 香1九, 歩1七. Gote: 歩1五 and a knight able to reach 2五, plus a bishop or rook placed differently from the column's ▲4四角 motif.
- Main line: no pawn in hand, knight first. Variation: the same position with one pawn in hand, so the sacrifice is now playable.

Ch4 「開いた端に香を重ねる」 (doubled lance and 田楽刺し on the edge):
- Mechanism: once the edge file is half open, a second lance dropped behind the first (香の重ね打ち) overloads the single defender. A lance dropped from far back can also pin or skewer two pieces standing on the edge file (田楽刺し, for example king and silver in a line).
- Also mention 下段の香 against dropping one rank higher to stop a knight drop, as a stated choice rather than a rule.
- Original position: a different material set from ch2/ch3. Gote has 玉1二 or 2一 with a silver on 1三. Sente has a lance in hand plus a lance on the file. Main line: the doubled lance breaks through. Variation: a 田楽 drop that wins the silver behind a pinned piece. Design a fresh line-up; do not reuse the yagura92 or anaguma-vol.2 layout.

Ch5 「受ける側：先に打つ歩と早逃げ」 (defender's view and when 手抜き is safe):
- Mechanism: the defender drops a pawn first on the square the attacker needs (敵の打ちたいところへ打て), or steps the king away early so that the edge break hits empty squares. An edge push can be ignored when the king is far from the edge or when the defender's counterattack is faster. This ties back to ch1's facing-pawns case.
- Original position: learner side gote, defending against a composed sente rook-and-lance battery on the 1筋. Main line: a pre-emptive pawn drop on 1四 followed by the king moving to 3一. Variation: passive play that lets the promotion through, for contrast.

Optional final check (quiz): use an app tsume (see tsume_candidates) where an edge-pawn push or edge pawn drop is the mating start. This links "端玉には端歩" to concrete mate.

sources.title: 打ち歩詰め (Wikipedia 日本語版)
sources.license: CC BY-SA 4.0 (consult for facts only; adapted: false per project rules)
facts: A pawn dropped from hand that gives check with no legal escape is a foul and the dropper loses; a pawn already on the board advancing to give mate (突き歩詰め) is legal.
A pawn drop that checks but is not itself mate is legal even if mate follows later.
Whether a pawn drop producing stalemate (no check) is a foul has no official ruling.
Earliest written codification is attributed to a 1636 rule book; the folk explanation about a pawn not taking the king's head has no documented basis.

In tsume problems the solver avoids a would-be pawn-drop mate by: giving the king a square (non-promotion of a rook/bishop/pawn, moving an own piece out of the way, sacrificing to open a square) or by letting the king or a defender capture the dropped pawn (shifting a defender, or blocking the line that protects the pawn).
Non-promotion of a bishop or rook has been used in real play to sidestep pawn-drop mate.

sources.title: 詰将棋 (Wikipedia 日本語版)
sources.license: CC BY-SA 4.0 (consult for facts only; adapted: false)
facts: Attacker moves first and must check each move; mate length is odd.
Defender chooses the longest defense; among equally long defenses, the one that makes the attacker spend more hand pieces is chosen.
Defender's hand is every piece not on the board, not in the attacker's hand, excluding kings; a piece type fully used cannot be dropped.
無駄合: an interposition captured for free that changes nothing is not counted; one that changes the sequence is a real defense.
Composed problems require a unique main line (other mates = 余詰) and no attacker pieces left over at the end (駒余り); 実戦型 problems relax decoration rules.
Length bands: under 7 moves is called ultra-short; up to 17 short; 19-49 medium; 51+ long. Since 2011 many beginner books focus on mates of 5 moves or fewer.
Named themes include 中合 (distant interposition that lengthens or changes the mate), 移動合, 限定合 (only one interposing piece type is correct), 邪魔駒消去, 打ち歩詰め回避, 不利先打, 限定打 vs 短打.
Quality terms: 作意 (intended line), 紛れ (tempting line that fails), 変化 (defender branch), 変化同手数, 非限定.

sources.title: 合駒 (Wikipedia 日本語版)
sources.license: CC BY-SA 4.0 (consult for facts only; adapted: false)
facts: An interposition places a piece between a long-range attacker (rook, dragon, bishop, horse, lance) and the king; it may be dropped from hand or made by moving a board piece (移動合), the latter keeping hand pieces or opening an escape square.
中合 (捨合) blocks away from the king to drag the checking piece closer, to let a further block follow, or to occupy a focal square.
The type of interposing piece can decide the result: a weak piece may stop a recapture from giving check, while a different piece type can enable the attacker's continuation.
Defenders often interpose cheap pieces (pawn, lance, knight) but the correct choice depends on what the attacker can do with the captured piece.

sources.title: 毎日詰将棋 (日本将棋連盟)
sources.license: All rights reserved (© Japan Shogi Association); problems not usable, rules summary consulted only
facts: The JSA publishes a daily problem; recent ones range from 3 to 11 moves, credited to professional composers.

Its rule summary: attacker checks every move, defender must answer every check, may interpose any piece except a king, plays the longest defense without 無駄合, and ordinary prohibitions (二歩, 打ち歩詰め, pieces with no further move, perpetual check) apply.

sources.title: ALSOK杯王将戦 将棋コラム 詰将棋
sources.license: Copyright © ALSOK CO.,LTD. All rights reserved; composed problems must not be reused
facts: Text commentary read via fetch; diagrams and hidden answer boards not inspected at full resolution.
5-move themes described: a gold sacrifice draws the king into a dangerous area and a silver sacrifice then seals its retreat before a dragon mates (lure + escape blocking).
When many first checks exist, the skill is choosing which major piece to give up and in what order.
Warnings: a natural first move can let the king slip out; a defender recapture can remove a supporting piece; choosing the wrong piece to fill a gap can lead into pawn-drop mate.

sources.title: ABC of Tsumi (Shogi Shack)
sources.license: All rights reserved (footer 2008~2025); reference only
facts: Text read via fetch; diagrams not inspected at full resolution.
Frames tsume as largely deciding which pieces to give up.
Its 5-move example is a 3-move finishing pattern preceded by one forcing sacrifice that the king must capture, i.e. a 5手詰 often equals sacrifice + known 3手詰 shape.
Before a drop, check whether the target square is guarded by a defender.

Unit id: endgame-mate5 (data/lessons/units/endgame-mate5.json). path ["上達のためのテクニック","終盤"], order 485 (free; sits after endgame-mate3 480, before endgame-mate-tesuji 490). Title idea ja 「五手詰：捨て駒で形を作ってから三手詰に入る」 / en "Mate in five: sacrifice to build the shape, then finish in three". Intro idea: a 5手詰 adds one forcing pair before a 3手詰; the extra pair usually changes where the king stands, which defender stands where, or what is in hand. Learner reads: no mate in 1/3 first → candidate checks including ones that hang a piece → every defender reply → remaining 3手詰. References (adapted:false): the three ja.wikipedia pages and the JSA page above; ALSOK/Shogi Shack only as 参考 if at all. Partial positions follow endgame-mate3 convention (sente king 9i, defender hand empty) except where a chapter needs defender drops.

Ch1 捨て駒で玉を呼び込む (lure). Mechanism: the first check is a piece the king must capture, pulling it onto a square where a knight check + drop mates. ORIGINAL composition, solver-verified this session (brute-force legal-move search with tsshogi): SFEN `6k2/4ng1L1/7+B1/9/9/9/9/9/K8 b BN 1` (gote K 3a, n 5b, g 4b; sente L 2b, +B 2c; hand B N). No mate in 1 or 3; unique key ▲2一香成 (forced promotion; lance cannot stay on rank 1), only reply △同玉; ▲1三桂 (unique), △1一玉 or △3一玉, both ▲2二角 mate; attacker hand empty at mate (no 駒余り). Steps: show why ▲2二角 now fails (king escapes via 2a/2b), the key, both branches as main + variation from step after ▲1三桂. Must still pass check-unit.ts originality and position checks.

Ch2 退路封鎖 (defender's own piece forced onto the escape square). Mechanism: sacrifice on the king's flight square that the king cannot take (guarded) so a defending gold/silver must capture and thereby plugs the square; then a 3手詰. Plan: compose a new position with king on rank 1/2, one defender gold or silver able to capture onto the flight square, attacker guard (knight/lance/horse) on that square; verify with engine/solver: no mate ≤3, unique key, all replies mated in 3, no 駒余り. Random search found this pattern rare; hand-compose by retracting from the desired final mate (final: king boxed by its own capturing piece, head-gold/drop mates). Include a variation showing the king-capture alternative fails because the square is guarded.

Ch3 打ち歩詰め回避. Mechanism: the obvious line ends with a pawn drop that would mate = foul; correct play gives the king one extra square (rook/bishop 不成) or lets the pawn be capturable, so the pawn drop is only check and the next move mates (or a different finish). Plan: compose with attacker hand containing P plus one piece; teach via a text step with dashed marks/arrow on the forbidden drop (validator rejects the illegal move, so never play it), then the 不成 line. Verify uniqueness and that the 成 version fails only because of 打ち歩詰め.

Ch4 合駒を数える: 5手詰 with long-range checks. Mechanism: when a rook/lance checks from distance, every interposing piece type is a separate defender reply; tsume convention picks the longest, and 限定合 means only one choice prolongs. Use app-owned computer-generated position m5-254 (allowed source: src/data/tsume.json) whose first move ▲9八香 (9i9h, capturing gold) allows eight drop replies; PV △9七歩 ▲同香 △9六歩 ▲8五金. Explain that captured interposed pieces enter the attacker's hand, and introduce the 限定合 term as a concept (no composed example copied).

Ch5 実戦型の五手詰を通して読む (practice). Use tsume.json m5-171 (double sacrifice: ▲1三金 captured by lance, ▲3三角成 captured by knight, ▲2二飛) or m5-200 (▲5二馬 sacrifice, △同玉 forced, ▲6三金, ▲5二銀), with variations for each defender reply listed below. Close with the 3手詰 vs 5手詰 summary: extra forcing pair; sacrifices are normal; check every defender reply including captures by non-king pieces and interpositions; hand changes after captures; 打ち歩詰め constraint.
